Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for Standardized ANCOVA Contrasts

Source: R/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.R
ss_aipe_sc_ancova.Rd

Sample size planning from the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) perspective for standardized ANCOVA contrasts.

Usage

ss_aipe_sc_ancova(
  true_contrast = NULL,
  true_sd_anova = NULL,
  true_sd_ancova = NULL,
  true_std_contrast = NULL,
  true_sd_ratio = NULL,
  true_cor = NULL,
  divisor = "s_ancova",
  c_weights,
  width,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  alpha_lower = NULL,
  alpha_upper = NULL,
  assurance = NULL,
  assurance_method = c("analytic", "simulation"),
  G = 10000,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_contrast

The population unstandardized ANCOVA (adjusted) contrast

true_sd_anova

The population error standard deviation of the ANOVA model

true_sd_ancova

The population error standard deviation of the ANCOVA model

true_std_contrast

The population standardized ANCOVA (adjusted) contrast

true_sd_ratio

The ratio of true_sd_ancova over true_sd_anova, greater than 0 and at most 1

true_cor

The population correlation coefficient between the response and the covariate

divisor

Which error standard deviation to be used in standardizing the contrast; the value can be either "s_ancova" or "s_anova"

c_weights

Contrast weights

width

The desired full width of the obtained confidence interval

conf_level

The desired confidence interval coverage (i.e., 1 - Type I error rate). Default is .95, which gives a symmetric two-sided interval, the interval ci_sc_ancova reports. A level above .999999998, whose tail areas are below 1e-9, is refused.

alpha_lower, alpha_upper

The lower-tail and upper-tail Type I error rates, an alternative to conf_level (give conf_level = NULL with them). ci_sc_ancova reports intervals with equal tail areas only, so the two must be equal, and alpha_lower = alpha_upper = a plans the interval of conf_level = 1 - 2a. Unequal values are refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid: they would plan for an interval no DMAR function reports. Each must be at least 1e-9: below it the noncentral t limits lose accuracy (see "Small tail areas" in ci_nc_t).

assurance

Parameter to ensure that the obtained confidence interval width is narrower than the desired width with a specified degree of certainty (must be NULL or greater than .5 and less than 1). An assurance above .999999998 is refused, with either assurance_method: the published assurance step finds noncentral t limits with tail areas of (1 - assurance) / 2, which must be at least 1e-9.

assurance_method

How the plan with assurance is made, used only with assurance. "analytic" (the default) is the published plan of Lai and Kelley (2012), computed without simulation, which does not compute the probability it attains and can attain less than assurance; assurance_attained is then NA. "simulation" returns the smallest sample size per group, at or above the plan without assurance, at which the probability that the ci_sc_ancova interval is no wider than width is at least assurance, with that probability estimated from G simulated samples and reported as assurance_attained (see Details).

G

Number of simulated samples at each sample size the assurance step tries, and in its estimate of the attained probability; a whole number of at least 100 (default 10000, which gives a Monte Carlo standard error of .004 for a probability of .80). Used and checked only with assurance and assurance_method = "simulation".

seed

Optional single number. When given, the assurance step is reproducible, and the random number stream of the calling session is left as it was. With NULL (the default) the draws come from the session's current stream. Used only where G is.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value: necessary_n_per_group, the per-group sample size needed for the planned ANCOVA contrast; with assurance, the rows assurance (the request) and assurance_attained: NA for the published plan of assurance_method = "analytic", which does not compute it, and for assurance_method = "simulation" the simulated probability at necessary_n_per_group that the ci_sc_ancova interval is no wider than width, with its Monte Carlo standard error in the attribute assurance_mc_se and the row G. With assurance the printed footer names the assurance method and says how assurance_attained was found, or that the published plan does not compute it; the attributes assurance_method and assurance_probability ("simulation" or "not computed") record the same.

Details

The sample size planning method this function is based on is developed in the context of simple (i.e., one-response-one-covariate) ANCOVA model and randomized design (i.e., same population covariate mean across groups).

An ANCOVA contrast can be standardized in at least two ways: (a) divided by the error standard deviation of the ANOVA model, (b) divided by the error standard deviation of the ANCOVA model. This function can be used to analyze both types of standardized ANCOVA contrasts.

Not all of the effect size arguments need to be specified. When divisor="s_ancova" the input is either (a) true_std_contrast, or (b) true_contrast (the unstandardized ANCOVA contrast) and true_sd_ancova. When divisor="s_anova", the valid input combinations are (a) true_std_contrast and true_sd_ratio; (b) true_std_contrast and true_cor; or (c) true_contrast, true_sd_anova, and true_sd_ancova. With divisor = "s_anova" the ratio of the two standard deviations, \(\sqrt{1 - \rho^2}\), must be greater than 0 and at most 1, as it is in every population (a covariate cannot raise the error variance), so true_cor of 1 or -1 is refused there.

The interval planned for. The plan is for the interval of ci_sc_ancova: the limits for the noncentrality parameter of a noncentral t on \(N - J - 1\) degrees of freedom at the observed t of the adjusted contrast, carried back to the scale of the standardized contrast by the standard error \(\sqrt{C/n + (\sum_j c_j \bar{X}_j)^2 / SS_{W,X}}\), with \(C = \sum_j c_j^2\), \(\bar{X}_j\) the covariate means, and \(SS_{W,X}\) the within-group sum of squares of the covariate (and, for the divisor "s_anova", by the ratio \(s_{ANCOVA}/s_{ANOVA}\)). The plan without assurance is for the criterion that this interval, evaluated at the planning value, is no wider than width (Lai & Kelley, 2012, Equations 21 and 28); it uses \(\sigma_{ANCOVA}\sqrt{C/n}\) as the standard error of the contrast, leaving out the covariate means term, which in a randomized design is small (Lai & Kelley, 2012, pp. 354–355). The plan is the smallest n per group that meets the criterion, searched from 2 per group, the smallest sample size with positive error degrees of freedom. The search doubles a step and then bisects, which finds the smallest n because the interval at the planning value narrows as n grows from 2 (checked at every n up to 80, and in steps of 10 up to 600, for 420 combinations of the contrast, the ratio \(\sigma_{ANCOVA}/\sigma_{ANOVA}\), weights for two to five groups, and the confidence level). At true_std_contrast = 0, c_weights = c(1, -1), and width = .5 the plan is 123 per group, where the interval is .49985 wide (.50190 at 122), and at true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .5, divisor = "s_anova", c_weights = c(1, -1), and width = 3.6 it is 2 per group, where the interval is 3.596 wide. A width that would need more than \(2^{53}\) (about \(9.0 \times 10^{15}\), the largest number up to which R holds every whole number exactly) per group is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid. The intervals have equal tail areas, as those of ci_sc_ancova do and as Lai and Kelley (2012, p. 354) assume.

Past about \(10^{11}\) per group the plan and assurance_attained are limited by the precision of doubles, as for ss_aipe_sc: the width changes by about \(1/(2n)\) of itself from one n to the next, and for a nonzero contrast it is the difference of two limits near the noncentrality. Against a 512-bit computation of the interval, with c_weights = c(1, -1), conf_level = .95, and the divisor "s_ancova", and with width and the tail areas as R holds them (each tail area, (1 - .95) / 2, is 0.025000000000000022 in doubles): at true_std_contrast = .5 and width of 1e-5, 1e-6, and 1e-7 the plan was 4, 1,035, and 525,379 above the smallest n that meets the criterion (about 3.2e11, 3.2e13, and 3.2e15 per group). At a contrast of 0, where the width is computed from the normal quantiles, the plan was the smallest n at width of 1e-3, 1e-5, and 1e-6 (about 3.1e7, 3.1e11, and 3.1e13 per group) and 2 below it at 1e-7 (about 3.1e15). Past about \(10^{15}\) per group the plan at a contrast of 0 can be below the smallest n, by up to about \(10^{-15} n\): at width = 6e-8 it is 8,536,575,157,098,048 per group, 8 below the smallest n, 8,536,575,157,098,056. With assurance = .9, assurance_method = "simulation", G = 200, and seed = 1, assurance_attained was the share of the same simulated statistics whose interval, computed in 512 bits, is no wider than width, up to 3.1e11 per group; at about 3.1e13 per group it was .950 where that share is .940 (contrast 0) and .900 where it is .895 (contrast .5), and at about 3.1e15 it was 1.000 where it is 0 (the plan is below the smallest n) and .905 where it is .930.

The assurance step. With assurance the plan is by default (assurance_method = "analytic") the published one (Lai & Kelley, 2012, pp. 358–359, a generalization of Kelley & Rausch, 2006): the value \(t^*\) that \(|T|\) does not exceed with probability assurance under the planner's model, carried back to the scale of the standardized contrast, is planned for without assurance. It is computed without simulation and does not compute the probability it attains, so assurance_attained is NA, and the printed footer says so. That model leaves out the covariate means term and treats \(s_{ANCOVA}/s_{ANOVA}\) as known, and the widths vary little, so the plan attains less than the request: at true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .5, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .5, and assurance = .80, the published plans (129 per group with divisor = "s_ancova", 98 with "s_anova") give an interval no wider than .5 with probability .77 and .55.

With assurance_method = "simulation" the plan is the smallest sample size per group, not below the plan without assurance, at which the ci_sc_ancova interval is no wider than width with at least that probability, for normal within-group errors and a normal covariate with the same distribution in every group (the randomized design). The width depends on the sample through five independent statistics: the contrast of the covariate means, the within-group sum of squares of the covariate, the contrast of the group means of the errors, the error of the pooled within-group slope, and the ANCOVA error sum of squares. The probability is estimated from G draws of these statistics from their exact sampling distributions, the same draws at every sample size the search tries, so that the estimate changes smoothly as the sample size grows, and both the covariate means term and, with divisor = "s_anova", the sampling of \(s_{ANCOVA}/s_{ANOVA}\) enter it. assurance_attained is the estimate at the returned sample size, at least assurance, with its Monte Carlo standard error in the attribute assurance_mc_se. Give seed for a plan that can be reproduced. For the divisor "s_anova", Lai and Kelley (2012, pp. 360–361) wrote that their assurance method is not appropriate, because the width varies with \(s_{ANCOVA}/s_{ANOVA}\) as well as with t, and gave as a practical solution an a priori Monte Carlo simulation that raises the sample size until the proportion of intervals no wider than the target reaches the assurance; this step is that simulation, made from the sufficient statistics rather than from raw data, and applied to both divisors. In the example above the simulated plans (130 and 104 per group, seed = 1) give an interval no wider than .5 with probability .87 and .84. Because the probability is estimated, a plan can differ by one from the smallest sample size at which the probability itself reaches assurance: with "s_anova" above, 103 gives .803. ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity simulates raw data at a plan, and the attained probability of any plan can be checked there.

References

Kelley, K. (2007). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Lai, K., & Kelley, K. (2012). Accuracy in parameter estimation for ANCOVA and ANOVA contrasts: Sample size planning via narrow confidence intervals. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 65, 350–370. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.2011.02029.x

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 9.)

Steiger, J. H., & Fouladi, R. T. (1997). Noncentrality interval estimation and the evaluation of statistical models. In L. L. Harlow, S. A. Mulaik, & J. H. Steiger (Eds.), What if there were no significance tests? (pp. 221–257). Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

See also

ss_aipe_sc, ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .8, width = .5, c_weights = c(.5, .5, 0, -1))
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 98   
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .8, true_sd_ratio = .6, width = .5,
                  c_weights = c(.5, .5, 0, -1), divisor = "s_anova")
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 39   
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .4, width = .3,
               c_weights = c(.5, .5, 0, -1), divisor = "s_anova")
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 221  
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# With assurance, the published plan of Lai and Kelley (2012), which
# does not compute the probability it attains.
ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .5, width = .5,
                  c_weights = c(1, -1), assurance = .90)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 130  
#>  assurance             0.900
#>  assurance_attained    <NA> 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; the plan is the published approximation, which does not compute the probability that the interval is no wider than the width (assurance_attained is NA) and can attain less than the assurance. assurance_method = "simulation" computes it and returns the smallest plan that attains it

# By simulation: the smallest sample size per group at which the
# interval is no wider than .5 with probability .90. G = 2000 keeps the
# example quick; a reported plan deserves the default G = 10000.
plan <- ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .5, width = .5,
                          c_weights = c(1, -1), assurance = .90,
                          assurance_method = "simulation",
                          G = 2000, seed = 113)
plan
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 131  
#>  assurance             0.900
#>  assurance_attained    0.930
#>  G                     2000 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: simulation; assurance_attained is estimated from G = 2000 simulated samples (Monte Carlo SE 0.006)
attr(plan, "assurance_mc_se")
#> [1] 0.005705261
